title: Le thé à l'anis étoilé  (Star-Anise Tea)

segments.t: Alone in a hotel room after Catherine leaves him, Mathias records a desperate voicemail begging his wife to let him come home, just before hotel reception calls up to announce that Camille is waiting downstairs. Camille invites her father to dinner, and over their meal in the hotel restaurant she tells him how she first fell in love with cinema. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Et Philippe, tu vois qui je veux dire?
Le frère de maman.
Oui, Philippe. Il avait un petit magasin de films.
J'avais treize ou quatorze ans, j'y allais tout le temps.
C'est là que j'ai découvert le cinéma.
Tu ne manges pas?
Je n'ai pas très faim.
Tu as mal au ventre? Prends du thé à l'anis étoilé.
Ce sont de petites étoiles qui sentent très bon.
C'est peut-être difficile à trouver à l'hôtel.
L'endroit est plutôt chic. Ils ont sûrement tout.
Au fait, tu as appelé Dominique Besnehard?
Non, pas encore. Pourquoi?
Je crois qu'Andréa préfère que tu restes.
Vraiment? Bonne nuit.
Bonne nuit, Camille.
Let's walk through the scene line by line. At the restaurant table, Camille talks about her childhood in the south.
Et Philippe, tu vois qui je veux dire?
'And Philippe, do you know who I mean?' Literally 'do you see who I want to say?'. In French, 'to want to say' is how you say 'to mean'.
Le frère de maman.
'Mom's brother.' He remembers her uncle right away.
Oui, Philippe. Il avait un petit magasin de films.
'Yes, Philippe. He had a little movie shop.' Camille explains that Philippe used to run a small video rental shop.
J'avais treize ou quatorze ans, j'y allais tout le temps.
'I was thirteen or fourteen, I went there all the time.' Remember that French uses 'to have' for age, and the tiny pronoun before 'went' means 'there'.
C'est là que j'ai découvert le cinéma.
'That's where I discovered cinema.' On weekends she would watch four or five films in a row.
Tu ne manges pas?
'Aren't you eating?' Camille asks a simple negative question in the present.
Je n'ai pas très faim.
'I'm not very hungry.' Literally 'I do not have very hunger'.
Tu as mal au ventre? Prends du thé à l'anis étoilé.
'Does your stomach hurt? Have some star-anise tea.' Literally 'do you have ache at the stomach?', a remedy she learned from her mother.
Ce sont de petites étoiles qui sentent très bon.
'They're little stars that smell very nice.' The verb for 'to smell' is followed by the adjective 'good' used as an adverb.
C'est peut-être difficile à trouver à l'hôtel.
'Maybe it's hard to find at the hotel.' Mathias doubts the hotel kitchen will have star anise.
L'endroit est plutôt chic. Ils ont sûrement tout.
'The place is quite fancy. They surely have everything.' Camille calls the waiter over and orders the tea for her father, along with the dessert menu for herself.
Au fait, tu as appelé Dominique Besnehard?
'By the way, did you call Dominique Besnehard?' Earlier, after firing Camille to appease his wife, Mathias had offered to help her find a job with the famous producer.
Non, pas encore. Pourquoi?
'No, not yet. Why?' This two-word phrase after 'no' means 'not yet'.
Je crois qu'Andréa préfère que tu restes.
'I think Andréa prefers that you stay.' Moved by his daughter's kindness, Mathias quietly gives her back her job at the agency.
Vraiment? Bonne nuit.
'Really? Good night.' Camille's face lights up with joy.
Bonne nuit, Camille.
'Good night, Camille.' He watches her walk away with a quiet smile.
Et Philippe, tu vois qui je veux dire?
Le frère de maman.
Oui, Philippe. Il avait un petit magasin de films.
J'avais treize ou quatorze ans, j'y allais tout le temps.
C'est là que j'ai découvert le cinéma.
Tu ne manges pas?
Je n'ai pas très faim.
Tu as mal au ventre? Prends du thé à l'anis étoilé.
Ce sont de petites étoiles qui sentent très bon.
C'est peut-être difficile à trouver à l'hôtel.
L'endroit est plutôt chic. Ils ont sûrement tout.
Au fait, tu as appelé Dominique Besnehard?
Non, pas encore. Pourquoi?
Je crois qu'Andréa préfère que tu restes.
Vraiment? Bonne nuit.
Bonne nuit, Camille.
With a cup of star-anise tea and a warm conversation about movies, Camille softens her father's heart and wins back her place at ASK. See you next time!
À bientôt!
